transform/case-study/karnataka-police-vp.description: India's first VPN-over-Broadband rollout, delivered by Rooman for Karnataka Police in 2010–11. Subsequently adopted by most Indian states.

blocks.html: India's first VPN-over-Broadband rollout, delivered by Rooman for Karnataka Police in 2010–11. Subsequently adopted by most Indian states.

h1.main: Karnataka State Police — VPNoBB. ₹34 crores → ₹4 crores. No loss of coverage. 1,400 stations.

rows: State in India to use VPNoBB

blocks.html: Karnataka Police operated 1,400 police stations, all connected to central data infrastructure via MPLS VPN. The annual connectivity cost was approximately ₹34 crores. On top of that, each station needed dedicated VPN hardware with associated maintenance costs. The architecture worked, but it was expensive, slow to scale, and inflexible.
The Department wanted a cheaper, more modern architecture without any degradation in coverage, reliability, or security.
Rooman proposed migrating from MPLS VPN to VPN-over-Broadband (VPNoBB). The design:

items: Replace expensive MPLS circuits with commodity broadband at each station.
Route all traffic through encrypted VPN tunnels to regional aggregation points.
Eliminate dedicated VPN appliances at each station — consolidate to the regional aggregators.
Maintain end-to-end encryption, audit trail, and access controls.

blocks.html: Annual connectivity cost dropped from ₹34 crores to ₹4 crores — an 88% saving. The additional hardware costs at each station also fell away. Coverage and reliability improved, as broadband had spread widely across India by 2010–11.
Karnataka became the first state in India to run the VPNoBB architecture for police infrastructure. Most other states have since adopted the same approach.

“Rooman's design reduced our operations cost to avail VPN connectivity from ₹34 crores to ₹4 crores per annum. This solution has also eliminated the cost for purchase and maintenance of devices across all the police stations in Karnataka. Karnataka is the first state to implement VPNoBB technology for connecting all the police stations; subsequently this technology is adopted in most of the states.”Sanjay Sahay, ADGP (retd), Karnataka State Police
